C-FIX-012-CURSOR-RESTORE-GUARD.Name: Skip cursor restoration when no complete cursor exists
C-FIX-012-CURSOR-RESTORE-GUARD.Summary: Complete FIX-012 at the ContentState post-render boundary by treating a null or endpoint-less cursor as having no selection to restore.
C-FIX-012-CURSOR-RESTORE-GUARD.Problem: After selector construction became cursor-safe, the complete registry walk rendered the cycled tab but ContentState.setCursor still forwarded an empty cursor to selection.setCursorRange, which dereferenced anchor.key and aborted the command.
C-FIX-012-CURSOR-RESTORE-GUARD.ApprovalBasis: This is the next narrow failing-evidence companion to the owner-approved C-FIX-012-TAB-CYCLE-RENDER work. It keeps the newly attributed ContentState restoration behavior explicit rather than silently broadening either prior plan.

Goals.Goal: Skip DOM selection restoration when cursor anchor/focus are absent.
Keep render-range derivation safe for null cursor state.

Constraints.Constraint: Do not synthesize cursor positions, mutate stored tab state, or catch downstream exceptions.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No selection subsystem rewrite, tab UX change, Windows/Linux work, release or publication.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: setCursor does not call selection.setCursorRange for null or incomplete cursor state.
A cursor with anchor/focus is forwarded unchanged.
The full registry walk completes without a tabs.cycleForward warning.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Direct selection-restoration fixtures and the complete browser command walk.
